newsitem.title: USA: U.S. will "probably" avoid trade war with EU.
newsitem.headline: U.S. will "probably" avoid trade war with EU.

text.p: President Clinton said on Thursday that the United States will "probably" avoid a trade war with Europe over the proposed $14 billion merger of Boeing Co. and McDonnell Douglas Corp., which the European Commission is threatening to block.

"There's an orderly process for our handling this and I think we'd better let the orderly process play itself out before we talk ourselves into a trade war," Clinton said in answer to a reporter's question at the White House. "I think we're a long way from that and I think we'll probably avoid it."
Clinton hinted that the United States might take some retaliatory action against Europe if it turns down the merger, or at least go to the World Trade Organisation.

"I'm concerned about what appear to be the reasons for the objection to the Boeing-McDonnell Douglas merger by the European Union," Clinton said. "And I think that it would be unfortunate if we had a trade stand-off with them.
"But we have a system for managing this through the World Trade Organisation and we have some options ourselves when actions are taken by Europe in this regard," he said.

A committee of European antitrust experts from the 15 European Union states advised the Commission on Wednesday to block the merger, agreeing with the Commission's competition services that Boeing had not fully met its concerns that the deal would threaten competition.
